title: 2007 AMC 12A 18
statement: The polynomial \(f(x)=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\) has real coefficients, and \(f(2i)=f(2+i)=0.\) What is \(a+b+c+d?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(f\) has real coefficients, the conjugates \(-2i\) and \(2-i\) are also roots. Thus \[ \begin{gathered} f(x) = (x^2+4)(x^2-4x+5) \\ = x^4-4x^3+9x^2 \\ {}-16x+20. \end{gathered} \]

Then \(a+b+c+d=-4+9\) \(-16+20\) \(=9.\) Equivalently, \(a+b+c+d=f(1)-1\) \(=(1+4)(1+1)-1\) \(=9.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Real coefficients force the conjugates \(-2i\) and \(2-i\) to be roots as well
